stories.headline: Trump Names Will Scharf as New White House Counsel Starting September 1
stories.summary:
President Trump has announced that Will Scharf, currently serving as White House staff secretary, will become White House counsel on September 1, replacing David Warrington. Scharf, 40, is a Harvard Law graduate and former federal prosecutor who represented Trump in the federal election obstruction case brought by special counsel Jack Smith. He is perhaps best known to the public as the official who explains Trump's executive orders before the president signs them.

The appointment is drawing significant attention ahead of the November midterm elections, with analysts noting Scharf's selection positions the White House for potential congressional oversight battles if Democrats regain control of one or both chambers. Republican strategist John Feehery told the Washington Examiner that Scharf "will be more aggressive" than his predecessor and is prepared for the anticipated clashes over subpoenas and document requests.

The White House has pushed back on characterizations that the change is purely defensive in nature. A White House official stated that the administration "is always prepared to respond to oversight requests, no matter who is in the House or Senate." Former House Oversight Chairman Jason Chaffetz described both outgoing counsel Warrington and Scharf as talented attorneys who hold the president's trust.

Scharf's appointment is backed by 22 outlets across the political spectrum, reflecting its broad significance. His background includes clerkships, violent crimes prosecution, and work helping confirm Supreme Court Justices Brett Kavanaugh and Amy Coney Barrett — experience that Republican observers say will prove critical if divided government returns after November.

stories.headline: Trump to Award Congressional Space Medal of Honor to Artemis II Crew on August 28
stories.summary:
President Trump will honor the four Artemis II astronauts — NASA's Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, along with Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen — with the Congressional Space Medal of Honor at a ceremony at NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston on August 28. The crew made history in April when their Orion spacecraft traveled 252,756 miles from Earth, surpassing the human spaceflight distance record set by Apollo 13 in 1970.

The Artemis II mission, which launched April 1 aboard NASA's Space Launch System rocket, was the first crewed lunar flyby in more than half a century. The crew passed within 4,067 miles of the lunar surface on April 6 and spent nearly 10 days in space, covering 695,081 total miles and capturing more than 7,000 images before splashing down in the Pacific Ocean on April 10.

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman noted the crew accepted "significant risk" in testing the Orion spacecraft and systems intended to carry future crews to the lunar surface. The agency aims to establish a permanent lunar base by 2028 as part of its broader Artemis program, with the mission seen as a critical stepping stone toward eventual crewed missions to Mars.

The ceremony marks formal recognition of one of the most significant American space achievements in decades, coming as the United States and China are engaged in a competitive race to return humans to the moon.

stories.headline: Update: Rescuers Search Ukraine Mall Rubble as Death Toll Rises to 16 After Russian Double-Tap Strike
stories.summary:
The death toll from a Russian double-tap drone strike on a shopping mall in Kryvyi Rih, Ukraine has risen to 16 after another body was retrieved from the rubble overnight, with nine people still missing including two children. More than 130 people were injured in the attack, which deliberately struck the mall in two waves — the second targeting emergency workers responding to the first strike. Twenty-three children were among the injured, with three in critical condition following surgery.

President Volodymyr Zelensky condemned the strike as "cynical and despicable," noting the deliberate targeting of rescuers. BBC-verified footage confirmed the second drone struck the already-burning mall during active rescue operations. Russian forces have not commented on the attack, which hit the hometown of the Ukrainian president.

Overnight exchanges continued across the conflict zone. Zelensky reported missile and drone strikes across multiple Ukrainian cities, including a fatal ballistic missile strike on railway infrastructure in Kyiv and a drone strike on a civilian minibus in Zaporizhzhia. Russian-held regions also reported Ukrainian strikes, with two children killed in Russia's Krasnodar region and two adults killed in Belgorod.

This is an update on the previously reported Kryvyi Rih mall strike: new details include the confirmed death toll rising to 16, the identities and conditions of critically injured children, ongoing rescue operations involving teams from seven Ukrainian regions, and overnight strikes by both sides.

stories.headline: Pakistan Supreme Court Orders Spark Imran Khan Hospital Visit, but Government Diverts Him to Different Facility
stories.summary:
Pakistan's former Prime Minister Imran Khan was returned to prison early Friday after an overnight medical examination, following a Supreme Court order that he be taken to a private hospital within 48 hours for assessment by specialists. A government-appointed team including an ophthalmologist, cardiologist, and general physician declared Khan "medically fit." However, authorities took him to a government-run facility rather than the private Shifa International Hospital specified in the court order, with officials citing security concerns created by PTI supporters gathering along the route.

Khan's party, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf, questioned whether the court order was fulfilled "in its true spirit," calling the substitution of hospitals a "superficial exercise for propaganda." The Supreme Court had also ordered Khan be allowed to see his family; his sister Noreen Khan visited him in prison Tuesday, and another sister accompanied him throughout the medical examination.

Khan, 73, has been imprisoned since August 2023 and faces charges in more than 100 cases ranging from corruption to leaking state secrets — charges he and his supporters characterize as politically motivated. His lawyers have raised concerns about deteriorating health, including claims that he has only 15% vision remaining in his right eye due to alleged prison authorities' failure to arrange specialist care, an allegation the government disputes.

The Supreme Court's intervention represents the most significant judicial relief Khan has received since his imprisonment, though critics argue the government's handling of the hospital transfer undermined the spirit of the order. The case continues to inflame tensions between the ruling coalition and Khan's PTI movement.
